arxiv-1809-05499.title: Elastic Registration of Geodesic Vascular Graphs
arxiv-1809-05499.creator: Stefano Moriconi (✉), Maria A. Zuluaga, H. Rolf Jäger, Parashkev Nachev, Sébastien Ourselin, M. Jorge Cardoso
arxiv-1809-05499.description: Abstract Vascular graphs can embed a number of high-level features, from morphological parameters, to functional biomarkers, and represent an invaluable tool for longitudinal and cross-sectional clinical inference. This, however, is only feasible when graphs are co-registered together, allowing coherent multiple comparisons. The robust registration of vascular topologies stands therefore as key enabling technology for group-wise analyses.

arxiv-2012-11073.title: Regularization in network optimization via trimmed stochastic gradient descent with noisy label Journal: Journal of Neurocomputing
arxiv-2012-11073.creator: Kensuke Nakamura 1 {}^{\text{1}}, Bong-Soo Sohn 1 {}^{\text{1}}, Kyoung-Jae Won 2 {}^{\text{2}}, Byung-Woo Hong 1 {}^{\text{1}}
arxiv-2012-11073.description: Abstract Regularization is essential for avoiding over-fitting to training data in network optimization, leading to better generalization of the trained networks. The label noise provides a strong implicit regularization by replacing the target ground truth labels of training examples by uniform random labels. However, it can cause undesirable misleading gradients due to the large loss associated with incorrect labels.

arxiv-2103-05660.title: Identifiability Analysis of Linear Ordinary Differential Equation Systems with a Single Trajectory Note: This work was funded in part by the National Institutes of Health under award number R01 AI087135 and the University of Rochester CTSA award number UL1 TR002001 from the National Center for Advan
arxiv-2103-05660.creator: Xing Qiu, Tao Xu, Babak Soltanalizadeh, Hulin Wu
arxiv-2103-05660.description: Abstract Ordinary differential equations (ODEs) are widely used to model dynamical behavior of systems. It is important to perform identifiability analysis prior to estimating unknown parameters in ODEs (a.k.a. inverse problem), because if a system is unidentifiable, the estimation procedure may fail or produce erroneous and misleading results.

arxiv-2309-05637.description: Abstract . Many existing systems track aliasing and uniqueness, each with their own trade-off between expressiveness and developer effort. arxiv-2410-20596.title: Practical Bayesian Algorithm Execution via Posterior Sampling
arxiv-2410-20596.creator: Chu Xin Cheng, Raul Astudillo *, Thomas Desautels, Yisong Yue
arxiv-2410-20596.description: Abstract We consider Bayesian algorithm execution (BAX), a framework for efficiently selecting evaluation points of an expensive function to infer a property of interest encoded as the output of a base algorithm. Since the base algorithm typically requires more evaluations than are feasible, it cannot be directly applied. Instead, BAX methods sequentially select evaluation points using a probabilistic numerical approach.

arxiv-2411-14284.title: Algebras for Deterministic Computation Are Inherently Incomplete
arxiv-2411-14284.creator: Balder ten Cate, Tobias Kappé
arxiv-2411-14284.description: Abstract . Kleene Algebra with Tests (KAT) provides an elegant algebraic framework for describing non-deterministic finite-state computations. Using a small finite set of non-deterministic programming constructs (sequencing, non-deterministic choice, and iteration) it is able to express all non-deterministic finite state control flow over a finite set of primitives.

arxiv-2502-13473.title: Multi-channel Replay Speech Detection using an Adaptive Learnable Beamformer
arxiv-2502-13473.creator: Michael Neri 1 {}^{\textbf{1}}, Member, IEEE, Tuomas Virtanen 1 {}^{\textbf{1}}, Fellow, IEEE
arxiv-2502-13473.description: Abstract Replay attacks belong to the class of severe threats against voice-controlled systems, exploiting the easy accessibility of speech signals by recorded and replayed speech to grant unauthorized access to sensitive data. In this work, we propose a multi-channel neural network architecture called M-ALRAD for the detection of replay attacks based on spatial audio features.

arxiv-2509-16860.title: LVADNet3D: A Deep Autoencoder for Reconstructing 3D Intraventricular Flow from Sparse Hemodynamic Data
arxiv-2509-16860.creator: Mohammad Abdul Hafeez Khan, Marcello Mattei Di Eugenio, Benjamin Diaz, Ruth E. White, Siddhartha Bhattacharyya, Venkat Keshav Chivukula
arxiv-2509-16860.description: Abstract Accurate assessment of intraventricular blood flow is essential for evaluating hemodynamic conditions in patients supported by Left Ventricular Assist Devices (LVADs). However, clinical imaging is either incompatible with LVADs or yields sparse, low-quality velocity data. While Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations provide high-fidelity data, they are computationally intensive and impractical for routine clinical use.

arxiv-2512-03318.title: Evaluating Generalization Capabilities of LLM-Based Agents in Mixed-Motive Scenarios Using Concordia
arxiv-2512-03318.creator: Chandler Smith, Marwa Abdulhai, Manfred Diaz, Marko Tesic, Rakshit S. Trivedi, Alexander Sasha Vezhnevets, Lewis Hammond, Jesse Clifton, Minsuk Chang, Edgar A. Duéñez-Guzmán, John P. Agapiou, Jayd Matyas, Danny Karmon, Dylan Hadfield-Menell, Natasha Jaques, Tim Baarslag, Jose Hernandez-Orallo, Joel
arxiv-2512-03318.description: Abstract Large Language Model (LLM) agents have demonstrated impressive capabilities for social interaction and are increasingly being deployed in situations where they might engage with both human and artificial agents. These interactions represent a critical frontier for LLM-based agents, yet existing evaluation methods fail to measure how well these capabilities generalize to novel social situations.

arxiv-2601-01760.description: Abstract Abstract Understanding natural phenomenon through the interactions of different complex systems has become an increasing focus in scientific inquiry. Defining complexity and actually measuring it is an ongoing debate and no standard framework has been established that is both theoretically sound and computationally practical to use.

pmc-11391766.creator: Juan José León, Nía Oetiker, Nicolás Torres, Nicolás Bruna, Evgenii Oskolkov, Pedro Lei, Andrey N Kuzmin, Kaiwen Chen, Stelios Andreadis, Blaine A Pfeifer, Mark T Swihart, Paras N Prasad, José Pérez-Donoso
pmc-11391766.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundRare-earth sulfide nanoparticles (NPs) could harness the optical and magnetic features of rare-earth ions for applications in nanotechnology. However, reports of their synthesis are scarce and typically require high temperatures and long synthesis times.ResultsHere we present a biosynthesis of terbium sulfide (TbS) NPs using microorganisms, identifying conditions that allow Escherichia coli to extracellularly produce TbS NPs in aqueous media at 37 °C by controlling cellular sulfur metabolism to produce a high concentration of sulfide ions.

pmc-12708749.creator: Pamela L Alebna, Sarah Martey, Anurag Mehta, Carl J Lavie, Salvatore Carbone
pmc-12708749.description: Purpose of reviewWhile excess adiposity is a known risk factor for incident heart failure ( HF), once the condition is established, observational data suggest that increased body mass index (BMI) may confer a survival advantage. This paradox has emphasized the underlying roles of cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF), and body composition, particularly lean mass (LM), in influencing clinical outcomes.

pmc-12951965.title: A spectral component approach leveraging identity-by-descent graphs to address recent population structure in genomic analysis
pmc-12951965.creator: Ruhollah Shemirani, Gillian M. Belbin, Sinead Cullina, Christa Caggiano, Christopher R. Gignoux, Noah Zaitlen, Eimear E. Kenny
pmc-12951965.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Population structure is a well-known confounder in statistical genetics, particularly in genome-wide association studies (GWAS), in which it can lead to inflated test statistics and spurious associations. Traditional methods, such as principal components (PCs), commonly used to adjust for population structure, are limited in capturing fine-scale, nonlinear patterns that arise from recent demographic events, patterns that are crucial for understanding rare variant effects.
